description: Machine-readable physics baselines transcribed from the tracked paper-analysis notebooks for use by the background-pairing intermediate report.

method_semantics.semi: Signal-informed CVaR25 model selection; an oracle benchmark, not a signal-agnostic method.
method_semantics.cap: Paper CAP model selection using empirical-CDF pairing.

missing_values.reason: The source notebook reports a dash because this method result is unavailable/collapsed; it is not zero.

epoch_metric_downstream_correlations.sign_convention: Spearman correlation with median downstream efficiency over common epoch steps. Stable and Wasserstein metric signs are inverted so larger always means better before correlation.

comparison_caveats: Compare paper CAP only with the new campaign's native-score CDF CAP control; mapping-based CAP is a different method variant.

Absolute CAP, Wasserstein, and drift values are not directly comparable because the paper compares combined ZeroBias with SingleNeutrino simulation, while the new campaign compares two recorded ZeroBias eras.
Native-score downstream efficiency over the same 20 anomalies and operating point is the primary paper-comparable outcome.
Semi is signal-informed oracle selection and must not be described as signal-agnostic.
Residual OAS for AE/VAE has no paper baseline and must be compared against native scores within the new campaign.

The six shared high-dimensional NSGA-II studies are screening studies, whereas the paper used independent two-objective M-TPE searches; sampler/front behavior is not directly paper-equivalent until targeted two-objective follow-up.
Missing q99 SVDD values must remain null and must not be imputed as zero.
The epoch correlations describe within-run metric/downstream co-movement over common epoch steps, not across-trial predictive validity.
